errors.evidence: I will compute the great‐circle distances between the capital cities of all ASEAN countries by first listing the 10 member states, their capitals, and the coordinates for each capital (sourced from Wikipedia). Notably, Indonesia’s capital, Jakarta, is the only ASEAN capital in the Southern Hemisphere (approximately –6.21° N, 106.85° E), while several ASEAN capitals lie well into the Northern Hemisphere. When examining the extreme cases, the combination of Jakarta with capitals in the northern part of ASEAN, especially those with a significant longitudinal separation, should yield the greatest distance. In comparing Jakarta to Hanoi (Vietnam) and Jakarta to Naypyidaw (Myanmar), the additional east–west difference (Jakarta being around 106.85° E and Naypyidaw around 96.08° E) shows that Jakarta–Naypyidaw is farther apart than Jakarta–Hanoi.
